newsitem.title: UK: UK Lib Dem leader says not despondent at polls.
newsitem.headline: UK Lib Dem leader says not despondent at polls.

text.p: Liberal Democrat leader Paddy Ashdown said on Tuesday he was not depressed by two opinion polls showing his party losing ground as the election campaign gets under way.

Ashdown said he was convinced that when voters realised that the Conservatives and Labour were offering similarly cautious policies on improving key services, they would start to come over to his party.
"They are wrong, and they have been wrong in the past," Ashdown said of a Reuter poll giving the Liberal Democrats 11 percent support and a Gallup poll showing them at 9.5 percent.

"Why look at the polls when you can look at real votes in real ballot boxes," Ashdown added, saying the Liberal Democrats had been running at close to 30 percent of the vote in local government by-elections held in recent weeks.
"If you measure our position now against our position months ago, or at this point before the last election, we are considerably improved," Ashdown told independent television.

"We are the only party offering a clear alternative -- Labour has now got so close to the Conservatives on many of the key issues that I don't know where they do stand on things like investment in education," he added.
